Terminology: paper round = 3 actions = engine turn; `round` in the context is the action slot 0..2.

rule_0_setup.description: Setup of a Dimension and of each player's deck. Tileset side depends on the player count (3x4 for up to 2 players, 4x4 for 3, 5x5 for 4 or more); every tile receives two face-down effects as traps and then one more card drawn from the shuffled monsters+skills pile. Each player draws 2 character cards and keeps 1, is dealt 10 effects and 4 skills (any of them may go to the archive instead of the deck), is dealt 2 class cards and keeps 1 (placed face up as the class permanent), then tops the deck up with A/B/M/P cards to at least 15 cards. Entry points are chosen in descending Will order; an entry tile may not hold a monster, may not be adjacent to a non-ally, and must be at least 2 tiles from any enemy; entering counts as a Move action (instants allowed) and the entry tile's traps still resolve. The engine evaluates these counts at turn 0 before the first action.

rule_1_actions_per_round.description: Turn economy. A character has exactly 3 actions per paper round (one engine turn), each chosen from Attack, Block, Move, Posture (or Empty Posture / Empty Move, Rule 6). A monster uses the action count printed on its card, 1 to 4; when an opponent has more actions than you, the surplus actions on your side are forced Empty Postures (and a forced EP may not be turned into an Empty Move). A player may delay entering the tileset and may cast permanents outside the Dimension so they are ready on the entry tile. The engine stores actions_per_round on every unit and derives the forced-EP count from the difference.

rule_2_discover_tile.description: Discovering a tile. A face-down tile turns face up ('open') the moment a unit Attacks it or Moves towards it. If a creature lies there it awakens (Rule 3) and the tile's effects become its hand. If only effects lie there the tile is a trap: every effect fires once against the discoverer with a power of 20 per element (pc ruling), i.e. trap power = 20 x number of trap elements; an element whose power does not exceed the defender's stat fails (Rule 18) and one failing element fails its whole effect (Rule 4). Context fields: tile.open, tile.creature, tile.effects (entry ids), tile.effect_elements (all elements of the trap effects).

rule_3_monster.description: Awakened creature behaviour. An awakened creature never leaves its tile (move distance 0) and attacks any enemy in contact (hex distance 1). All effects lying on its tile form its hand; its actions are rolled on D6 (Rule 5). While no enemy is in contact the creature regenerates. The creature is steered by the next enemy player in seating order (the player after the one in contact). Context: target is the creature (target.kind == 'creature', target.awake), dist the caster-creature distance.

rule_4_traps.description: Trap resolution. A trap (open tile with effects and no creature) is disabled once all of its effects have failed to kill or lock the discoverer: the discoverer survives the damage and is not locked. An effect fails as a whole as soon as one of its elements fails, i.e. when the trap power (20 per element, Rule 2) does not exceed the defender's stat behind that element. All traps resolve within one round. A kill or lock costs the character one re-entry attempt (a 'time'); the character may re-enter and fight for a draw.

rule_5_monster_dice.description: Monster actions by dice. A creature in contact with a character rolls 4 D6 per action (or its printed pattern such as BAAPM / AAAM, one die per letter) and acts on the colour that scores highest: green = Block, blue/white = Move, red = Attack, black = Posture. When Posture wins the creature picks an effect from its hand and stops rolling until all of that effect's elements are emitted (one per action). Context: caster is the creature, caster.dice_pattern its optional printed pattern, die_face the winning colour, cast.step/of the running emission.

rule_6_empty_posture_move.description: Empty Posture / Empty Move. EP is the no-op action: it gains no matrix edge (pc: 'EP no benefits'), may still emit an element, and always returns to the hand. The same card may be declared first as Empty Move: the unit advances halfway toward its target (ceil(dist/2) hexes). For the resolution matrix the enemy picks the empty type that hurts the empty actor: Attack treats EP as Posture (A vs EP = 2), Posture treats EP as Empty Move (P vs EP = 1), Block treats EM as Move (B vs EM = 1); Move/Block vs EP are neutral. A forced EP (Rule 1/7) may not be converted into EM. Reaver exception (pc): its EP and EM fight as Attack.

rule_7_turn_round_sequence.description: Turn structure. Units in contact commit their action cards face down simultaneously each action; cards flip, instants and skills may still be played, targets are pointed out and the resolution matrix applies: base 1 damage for Attack plus 1 per edge (A>P/EP, P>M/EM/EP, M>B, B>A), so A vs P = 2 and B vs A = 1 to the attacker. Effects are emitted only on P/EP. After the third action of the engine turn, characters may discard and draw up to 5 (Rule 10); monsters never discard. A unit facing an opponent with more actions per round fills the gap with forced Empty Postures.

rule_8_card_declare_sequence.description: Declaration order within an action: (1) Empty Move, (2) the action card (A/B/M/P/EP), (3) effects — a declared effect binds this action to emit its next element, (4) skills, instants, class abilities OR a point-buy against a token (Rule 24). There is no stack: everything applies, prohibitions are applied last as replacements. Pc override: instants are committed with the action; if the action's maths gave the player no benefit (took no less, dealt no more, healed no more than without the instant) the instant returns to the hand instead of being discarded, in bonus rounds too (rule_8_instant_returns). rule_9_class_card.description: Class card. On entering a Dimension the class card is in play as a permanent with a token of fixed value 6 per colour (no point-buy at placement). rule_10_draw.description: Draw. rule_11_archive.description: Archive. Instead of discarding, a used card may be moved to the archive, but only while the cards still in circulation (deck + discard + hand + holding) stay at or above 15 afterwards (deck_floor; pc: the deck never goes below 15). Defeated creatures' cards also live in the archive and can be used by Summoning / Possess / Resurrect as outer-dimension allies: such an ally enters on its owner's tile, moves with the owner and is steered like a player-managed monster. An archived card may always be moved back to the discard pile. Context: caster.circulating_cards, card (entry id), card_kind.

rule_12_permanent_types.description: Permanents and tokens. A small neutral die over the permanent shows the lowest colour value. Token kinds: tile token (big coloured die right of the tile, bonus to every creature there), permanent token (coloured die over a stat, added), stat-penalty token (wooden die under a stat, subtracted), shield token (Rule 20). Context: card (effect id), dice (the roll), permanent.tokens.

rule_14.description: Rule 14 in three parts. A — acquisition/trade: effects and skills are acquired by conquering a tile or from a defeated character's deck and go to discard or archive; adjacent characters may trade archives for an action when one of them moves towards the other, and may discard into each other's piles. B — life: life = round_half_up(sum of stats / 10) (life_from_stats): every character has 40 -> 4, a Dragon 80 -> 8; the life die is recalculated whenever damage is taken or a token of value 5 or more is added to the tile or character. C — adjacency: a unit may only be attacked from the surrounding tiles (paper: 8 neighbours; engine: hex distance 1, in_contact).

rule_15_target_follow.description: Targeting. Attack and Move target one enemy or tile; Posture and Block are untargeted (pc), Block dealing 1 to each enemy who attacked you (B > A edge). Pc target priority when no explicit target: (1) the enemy against whom I take less damage, (2) an enemy that would take damage, (3) the enemy with the lowest life; a right-clicked target is honoured when in contact. Score = 100 x i_take_less + 10 x enemy_takes_damage - life, highest wins. Two units Moving to the same tile: only the one truly using Move arrives; on mirrored Moves nobody moves. An attacker may follow a target that moves away. Context: candidate.{i_take_less, damage_to_enemy, life}, caster.move_target, defender.move_target.

rule_18_element_emit.description: Element emission. Each element of an effect is emitted with power equal to the caster's stat behind it (stat_of via elements.json: Vitality; World for souls/time/space; Matter for air/water/earth/fire; Will for concentration/harmony) and resisted with the defender's same stat. An element whose power does not exceed the defender's stat fails (deals 0 on that element; a non-damage effect is saved). Point-buy effects cannot be resisted. The current element is elements[cast.step]. Pc Counter Spell: one element type, subtract my stat from theirs per instance. Disabled elements (Disable) may not be emitted.

rule_19_effect_cast.description: Casting by contiguous Postures. A non-instant effect emits one element per Posture / Empty Posture, in the card's order; any other action between two emissions interrupts the cast (pc: the cast fails and the card is discarded), except that Move does not interrupt a class that may emit on Move (Monk). rule_20_effect_types.description: Effect types and the point-buy. Types (valid_effect_types): damage (Rule 21 stat comparison), point-buy (dice, unresistable), instant (any action), shield token (die over the tile as extra life, cumulative), channeling (temporary permanent, lost when channeling stops or its last token dies), stat buy (bank the stat per emission until the card's total, stat_buy_paid). Point-buy: roll point_buy_dice_count(stat) d6; the roll fits when the sum is at most the stat (point_buy_succeeds); keep the highest die (point_buy_token_value) as token or damage. Pc: the point-buy is per emission and a failed roll re-emits only that element next action; once a non-instant effect is picked only P/EP/EM remain selectable; Fireball deals delta damage and leaves a fire tile token; Force Shield is permanent and its Vitality die is subtracted from the effect sum. Context: dice (this roll), cast.non_instant_selected.

rule_21_effect_damage.description: Effect damage. Damage applies when the defender has no tokens left to destroy; otherwise the defender chooses a token to lose instead. Pc Dodge: 1 less combat damage in total. Implemented as rule_21_delta_damage; life uses the same rounding (life_from_stats).

rule_24_destroy_permanent_token.description: Destroying permanents and tokens. Pc: on a Posture / Empty Posture the caster emits a stat (one point-buy of one of the token's elements) against the closest adjacent enemy's permanents; a die at least the token's power destroys it (using_rule_24); fixed-power permanents (class card, summons, golems, elementals, resurrect) need a 6 (fixed_power_6); the class card itself can never be destroyed. Without an Aura permanent a caster either emits an element or targets exactly one permanent/token, not both. Target order (user ruling 2026-11-14, peer.mjs candidatesOf → effects.mjs rule24Order): of the adjacent enemy (sorted ids; a Possess in an adjacent ally's holding first) the emission takes its permanents first, then its character stat bonus tokens (Artifice, a broken Fortress …), then the bonus tile tokens under it — stable inside a class. Context: token.{power, fixed, is_class_card, kind}, die, cast.aura, cast.emitting, target.permanents.

rule_building_fortress.description: User ruling 2026-11-14 (supersedes the 2026-11-12 "stat above its value, any good roll breaks it"); bonus re-ruled 2026-11-14 #2 ("Highest die. Just a bonus stat token, just like the one that Artifice generates … destroyable the same way"). js/building-bonus.js: the fortress value = data.fortress.stat_min + floor(hex roll × (stat_max − stat_min + 1)) (30..60, deterministic per hex; its stat = the building's stat hint / hash as before). peer.mjs fortressStatBuy (inside the Rule 24 destroy loop, reveal `destroy: { stat, building: "q,r" }` on P / EP): within data.fortress.near, once per data.fortress.per (action | turn), bank += my current stat of that kind (stat buy, no roll); bank ≥ value → broken: world edit `bld:q,r` gone (applied by the breaker, read by everyone), dice = round(value / bonus_divisor) from the reveal salt, bonus = the HIGHEST die (data.fortress.bonus max | sum). applyFortressOutcomes puts it in my stat_tokens_json as a character stat bonus token — exactly Artifice's kind: { stat, elem = first element (sorted ids) behind the stat (fortressTokenElem), value, effect_id: rule_building_fortress }, one positive token per element (effects.mjs placeStatBonusToken: a new one replaces an earlier one of that element only if higher; stacks with an Artifice token of another element). It counts in my stat, my life maximum (Σ/10 rule) and the UI token modifier like any stat token, and falls under Rule 24: an adjacent enemy emitting that stat against me takes my permanents first, then my character stat bonus tokens (this one), then the bonus tile tokens under me (rule24Order); a die ≥ the token value destroys it. Snapshot: fortress_bank_json { id, stat, value, bank, turn, action }; the old fortress_bonus_json is no longer written (ignored if an older peer sends it). Another unit breaking it voids my bank. Lifetime (user ruling 2026-11-15: "permanent token from the highest die"): the token is permanent — no turn / round / action end, snapshot rebuild or later token of that element that is not higher takes it; only Rule 24 (as above) or my death removes it (peer.mjs DIED branch drops my Fortress tokens; a Resurrect does not bring them back); tokens are not kept when a save is loaded. The breaker gets a HUD notice with the dice and the token. UI: the stat-buy button shows the peer-queued emission (hand msg destroy), which the peer clears after every action — stat-buy again each action.

rule_monster_deck_effects.description: User rulings 2026-11-15 ("can you make the monsters to hold in deck 4 effects and to cast them." + "let the monsters have 2 more random effects, besides the 4 effects mix they have."). A monster = a wild creature (npc side, not a companion / summon). peer.mjs deck build: 11 action cards + 4 skills + data.monster_deck.thematic effect cards = the creature version's deck_effects (data/creatures.json, chosen once by game/monster-deck.mjs pickThematicEffects: AI-castable — none of ai_exclude_keys / ai_exclude_effects —, affordable under monster_effect_affordable with max_len / min_stat / min_stat_delta, mix 2 damage + 1 defence + the best remaining) + data.monster_deck.random random playable effects (pickRandomEffects, seed sha256(map seed : peer label : creature id : k), distinct from each other and from the thematic ones, need not be affordable) — 21 cards, above DECK_MIN 15. Logged as `monster deck: <creature> thematic [...] + random [...]`. They circulate like any card (draw, hand, discard, reshuffle; dropDeathCard may drop one). npcPlan (once awake): a cast in progress goes on with Posture / Empty Posture, never a move (Rule 19), aimed at the nearest enemy; else npcCastChoice over the hand — damage on an enemy within the effect's reach (delta only if it hurts), defence with an enemy within threat_range, control on an enemy in contact, Meteor Shower only when more enemies than allies are within 10 and life ≥ 3 — each with chance cast_chance[kind] from the monster's own RNG; otherwise the old weighted A/M/P/B pick. An effect card it can never use (not AI-castable or not affordable) goes back to its discard pile when its hand holds no action card. User ruling 2026-11-15 ("Should allied npc_a heroes and summons also cast their effect cards? -> Yes, they should do"): with data.monster_deck.ally_cast every other bot-driven non-human unit (npc_a / npc_c heroes, companions, summons, bound creatures; never HUMAN / profile heroes played by a person) casts the effect cards of its OWN deck through the same npcCastChoice (ally mode) — same pool / affordability / cast_chance, never moving while casting; a companion keeps a running cast even when its owner walks off and starts one only next to its owner; Turn Life heals the most hurt friend in contact (at half life or less, or when nobody in reach can be hurt and it is worse off than the caster); Meteor Shower needs more enemies within 10 than its side counting itself (owner and allies). Potion Brew (self_or_ally) goes on the friend in contact it helps more than the caster (lower life share, or the same share and a smaller life max); planning keeps a pointed unit for self_or_ally / self_or_enemy effects in the reveal (players too), effects.mjs falls back to the caster when it is not allied / in contact. Ally-mode affordability (monster deck_effects unchanged): ally_min_stat per element, ally_min_stat_delta delta mean, and with heal_ignores_delta a heal (Turn Life) needs no delta mean, only round(Vitality/10) >= 1. Rule 8: a heal my cast gives an ally counts as a benefit (user ruling 2026-11-15). The stuck-card rule applies to them too (their hand can fill with cards the AI never casts the same way).

rule_monster_natural_permanents.description: User rulings 2026-11-15 ("A monster's natural effect becomes a card with a Permanent type. Each such monster starts with 2 copies of it already cast as permanents, power 6 each (Rule 24), held in play, with no further copies in its deck"). peer.mjs boot (IS_MONSTER only — wild creatures; companions, summons, human / npc_b heroes excluded): naturalPermFor(creature data) → entity.permanents.add(id), permPower[id] = data.natural_permanents.power, permCopies[id] = data.natural_permanents.copies (snapshot perm_copies_json), that many effect cards pushed into heldCards (counted by circulating() for DECK_MIN), the id excluded from the thematic / random deck picks (destroyed copies are archived, so the card never circulates and npcCastChoice never sees it). Natural Spirit Link: 2 copies standing = ∀ (all four stats linked), 1 copy = Vitality. Logged `natural permanents: <name> ×2 (power 6 each)`. Two copies = one id + a count, so every Set-by-id reader (Rule 24 candidatesOf / permStats via element_cost, hasPerm, Delay-Time-style readers of permanents_csv, the perms strip, dropPermanent, heldCards) stays correct: Rule 24 destroying it takes ONE copy (dropPermanent decrements and moves that copy's held card to the ARCHIVE — out of circulation, user answer 2026-11-15; the last copy drops the permanent). A restart / rejoin / ghost replacement (START_LIFE) boots a fresh process with exactly the configured copies — never doubled. Semantics per effect (data.natural_permanents.effects): turn_tick Earthquake, ward Creation, link Spirit Link, spare_holder Love / Awe, no_damage Fear, only_holder Anger, lose_action Domination, stone Petrify, no_attack Mists — see each effect's logic and game/natural-perms.mjs.

rule_unattended_character.description: User ruling 2026-11-16 (revised): heroes without owner (character_id, no owner_peer_id) silent for data.unattended.silence_ms (60000 since 1.1.0, user ruling 2026-11-27 — the minute of rule_unit_standin; env SHADOW_MS shortens it for tests) become unattended: peer.mjs - run by the live hero with the smallest peer id, never by an unattended one - spawns an ordinary peer process (spawnCompanion wild, no owner) with SHADOW_OF = the hero's peer id, REPLACES_PEER_ID = the silent peer, ALLY_OF = its ally-join link, CHARACTER_ID / ENTITY_NAME / ALLIANCE / FORCE_CLASS / START_LIFE / SHADOW_STATS_JSON from its last snapshot, on its tile. It is not HUMAN: npcPlan plays it as an allied bot. Master (unattendedLeader): a group mate's live master is kept (sticky), else the live, alive human character of its link group (ally_of edges, same side) with the earliest joined_at (tie: peer id); published as led_by (followers) and leader (master). With a master npcPlan uses the summon owner-follow branch (walk next to it, fight what is in contact); without one it holds: npcCast / fight in contact, else Posture / Block. Takeover: the returning player (restore-here / restore / rejoin / a unit-list join of that profile character) boots with REPLACES_PEER_ID = the unattended peer and its life, ALLY_OF empty (it leaves the group); killed = dead there (death card: shadow_death, game/shadow-settle.mjs). Vanish: no living attended character (or its master) within data.unattended.vanish_radius for data.unattended.vanish_after_ms (env UNATTENDED_VANISH_MS for tests) -> it publishes out, pushes its Door and exits; receivers drop it, join-plan.mjs doorRecords drops out records (no longer alive there).

rule_unit_standin.description: User ruling 2026-11-27 (S6): peer.mjs, run by the live hero with the smallest peer id every 10 s, finds a monster or villager (creature_id; not owned, not summoned, not built-in, not a follower or a villager walking home) whose last snapshot is older than data.standin.silence_ms (GHOST_MS) and spawns its STAND-IN: a wild monster through spawnCompanion, a villager through spawnVillager (its village, NPC, home; on the phone within VILLAGE_MAX_MOBILE), with STANDIN_OF = the original peer id (a silent stand-in passes its own original on), REPLACES_PEER_ID = the silent peer, START_LIFE, on its tile. UNIT_LABEL (the original label) keeps what the unit derives from its label (village slot, builder post, recruit edits, monster deck); observers read unitLabelOf(snapshot). Hand-back: the original hearing a snapshot with standin_of = itself (standinSeen) takes the tile and life, names the stand-in in replaces; the stand-in hearing replaces = itself steps down (shadowStepDown); every peer keeps the replaced side out (supersededBy). Since 1.1.0 (user answer 2026-11-27) the summoner also stands in for its own spawned creature (Summoning, Golems, Elementals) while it holds the permanent: the same creature for the same permanent; its summons list names the stand-in and swaps back on the hand-back.
